title: Matched Capabilities, Different Behaviors: A Controlled Study of MCP and CLI Interfaces for Language Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.34298v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language agents increasingly act through external tools and interactive environments, making the interface between the model and its executable capabilities part of the decision process. Model Context Protocol (MCP) and command-line interfaces (CLI) can expose the same semantic operations through markedly different model-facing representations. We study whether these representational differences change agent behavior when executable capabilities are matched. We introduce Matched Interface Comparison and Analysis (MICA), which renders MCP and CLI from a shared semantic action contract and routes decoded actions through the same runtime. Across six models and three interactive environments, matched interfaces produce substantial differences in task performance and interaction cost. translated_title: 匹配的能力，不同的行为：面向语言智能体的MCP与CLI接口的受控研究
translated_abstract: 语言智能体越来越多地通过外部工具和交互环境来执行操作，这使得模型与其可执行能力之间的接口成为决策过程的一部分。模型上下文协议（MCP）和命令行界面（CLI）可以通过截然不同的面向模型的表示形式暴露相同的语义操作。我们研究在可执行能力相同的情况下，这些表示差异是否会改变智能体的行为。我们提出了匹配接口比较与分析框架（MICA），该框架从共享的语义动作契约渲染出MCP和CLI，并将解码后的动作路由到相同的运行时。在六个模型和三个交互环境中，匹配的接口在任务性能和交互成本上产生了显著差异。这些影响不仅限于表面有效性，还延伸到语义动作选择、失败路径和恢复过程。匹配状态探针将敏感性定位于能力……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出MICA框架，在共享语义动作契约下对MCP和CLI进行受控对比，发现即使可执行能力完全相同，接口表示差异仍会显著影响语言智能体的任务性能、交互成本、动作选择、失败路径与恢复行为。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MICA, a controlled comparison framework that renders MCP and CLI from a shared semantic action contract, showing that even with matched executable capabilities, interface representational differences substantially affect language agents' task performance, interaction cost, semantic action selection, failure pathways, and recovery.
